c74object.name: analyze~
c74object.digest: Performs spectral transience analysis on an audio signal
c74object.description:
The `analyze~` object performs real-time spectral analysis of an incoming audio signal. It utilizes an STFT-based Mel-spectrogram and Spectral Flux to detect transient peaks and calculate various transience-related metrics. The analysis is performed on a 1ms-hop basis and utilizes a background thread for expensive calculations to maintain audio stability.
This object uses a unified 15.2-second stateful analysis window, ensuring parity with offline Python-based analysis. Transients are detected across four frequency bands (Sub, Bass/Low-Mid, High-Mid, Treble) and assigned a "Resonance Score" based on their historical relationship with other peaks in a 5-second lookback buffer. The adaptive midpoint threshold for peak detection is calculated using a specialized dynamic historical peak-based sub-window.

inlet.description: Accepts the audio signal to be analyzed.

Accepts a signal representing the current transport clock time. This value is buffered and used to provide compensated timestamps for detected peaks. If no signal is connected to this inlet, the object maintains backwards compatibility and omits the clock value from its output.

outlet.description: Outputs a list whenever a transient peak is detected. If a signal is connected to the second inlet, the list contains three elements: [compensated clock value, band index, transience score]. If no signal is connected, it outputs the legacy two-element list: [band index, transience score].
Outputs the bar length (ms) determined from the analysis history histogram, optionally using a weighted calculation if `@weighted_bar` is enabled.
Outputs the average rating score calculated over the analysis history.
Outputs the current standard deviation of the analysis scores.
Outputs a score representing the spectral contrast detected in the signal.

Outputs a score representing the stability of the rhythmic center. It maintains a histogram of the frequency of "highest peak" positions (Bar Lengths). The output value is the average of the counts for all Bar Length integers observed during the current analysis session. A higher value indicates a more stable rhythmic center.

method.name: clear
method.description: Clears the internal historical buffers, including the cumulative transience history and the audio/clock buffers. All calculated metrics (Rating, Standard Deviation, etc.) are reset to their initialized values. If the object is part of a shared group, the shared group's buffer is also cleared.

method.name: pause
method.description: Pauses or resumes transience analysis for specified 1-based audio channel numbers. Accepts a list of one or more integers representing channel numbers to pause. Sending `pause 1` pauses analysis for `analyze~`'s channel. Sending `pause 0` resumes analysis for all channels as normal.

attribute.name: active
attribute.description: Enables or disables object processing. When active is enabled (1, default), the object has full normal functionality. When active is disabled (0), the object consumes zero CPU/network resources and performs no DSP analysis or visualizer spawning until set back to active (1).

attribute.name: group
attribute.description: Sets the name of the shared memory group. Objects with the same group name will share a cumulative history buffer, allowing their transience analysis to be context-aware of each other. This enables inter-stream rhythmic reinforcement and global transience density calculations. If no group is specified, the object uses a private buffer. Note: This attribute can only be set during object instantiation.

attribute.name: log
attribute.description: Enables or disables detailed diagnostic logging. When enabled (1), internal analysis states, peak detection events, and performance metrics are sent to the rightmost outlet. This is useful for debugging and fine-tuning the analyzer's behavior.

attribute.name: weighted_bar
attribute.description: Enables or disables the weighted multiplier applied when finding the bar length to output from the object. When enabled (1, default), the output bar length is determined by finding the bar length in the histogram that maximizes the count multiplied by a weight equal to the bar length divided by 5000. When disabled (0), the output bar length is determined by simply finding the bar length with the highest count in the histogram.

attribute.name: tolerance
attribute.description: Defines the snapping tolerance in milliseconds for historical qualifier calculations (default 29.0 ms). When processing each qualifier, the analyzer searches within a window of 2*tolerance (one tolerance on each side) of the qualifier's original position to find the highest accumulated value in the 5-second buffer and snaps the qualifier to that peak.

attribute.name: visualize
attribute.description: Enables or disables real-time visualization. When enabled (1), the object automatically launches the companion visualizer process (transience_vis.py) in the background and streams highly detailed, real-time transient analysis frames (including 4-band envelopes, dynamic smoothings, peak scoring markers, metrics, and the 5-second accumulated historical buffer) over localhost TCP port 9001. When the object instance is freed (e.g. when deleted or when Max closes), any active visualizer processes spawned by the object are automatically closed.
